source_title: Maine BMV Motor Carrier Services — Overlimit Permits (29-A M.R.S. §2382; Motor Carrier Rules Ch. 156/157/164)
verify_reasons: Official Maine BMV overlimit-permit page confirms pilot-vehicle triggers at width over 12', length over 80', and 15'+ rear overhang, plus the single-trip fee range and travel windows; the higher width police-escort thresholds (over 16' = 1 pilot + 1 police, over 20' = 2 police) and the height-over-16' pole-car rule are cross-referenced from published permit summaries of Maine Motor Carrier Rules Ch. 156/157/164, not read verbatim from the official page — confirm exact configuration with Maine MCS (207-624-9000 x52134).

Maine publishes no fixed numeric 'superload' dimension/weight threshold; very heavy loads are individually reviewed (bridge analysis) — superload_thresholds left null (handler raises a verify flag, does not auto-assert superload).

superload_thresholds.note: Maine does not publish a fixed superload dimension/weight threshold. Loads at/over 16' wide require police escort and extreme loads are individually route-/bridge-reviewed by Maine MCS. Null values flag the load for manual superload verification rather than clearing it.

width.note: 1 pilot vehicle over 12' wide — front on 2-lane, rear on divided highway
over 16' wide: 1 pilot car + 1 police escort (per published Maine permit summaries — confirm with MCS)
over 20' wide: 2 police escorts (per published Maine permit summaries — confirm with MCS)

height.note: over 16' high: pilot car with height pole (per published Maine permit summaries — confirm with MCS)

length.note: 1 pilot vehicle over 80' overall length; also 1 pilot when rear overhang is 15' or more

single_trip.fee_formula: Secretary of State sets the single-trip overlimit fee at not less than $6 and not more than $30 based on weight, height, length and width (29-A M.R.S. §2382). Maine Turnpike oversize/overlength permit = $10 at any toll plaza (plus toll).
single_trip.note: Single-trip overlimit permit valid 7 days. 'Oversize Load' signs + 18" flags required on overwidth/overlength loads.

annual.note: Annual/blanket overlimit permits available for qualifying repetitive/divisible moves; fee set by SOS schedule — quote through Maine MCS.

movement_restrictions: Travel permitted one-half hour before sunrise to one-half hour after sunset, 7 days a week
No travel on weekends during July and August
No travel on major holidays / some holiday weekends
Two-way communication required between the overlimit vehicle(s) and pilot/police escort(s) at all times
Non-reducible loads may exceed 13'6" height up to 14'0" off the Maine Turnpike; Turnpike oversize/overlength permits obtained at toll plazas
notes: Legal limits: width 8'6", loaded height 13'6" (up to 14'0" for non-reducible loads off the Turnpike), gross 80,000 lbs; 53' semitrailer on the National Network.

Escort width/length triggers and travel windows confirmed from the official Maine BMV overlimit-permit page; fee range from 29-A M.R.S. §2382. Higher width/height escort thresholds cross-referenced from published Maine permit summaries.
State-level rules only — municipal permits, bridge-specific engineering and low-clearance routing are out of scope.
